claims.text: An AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating can effectively adhere to a copper matrix.
A graded Ni-based interlayer promotes adhesion between an AlCoCrFeNi coating and a copper matrix.
The graded Ni-based interlayer produces a diffusion-driven transitional layer.
The transitional layer mitigates thermal-expansion mismatch between the coating and copper matrix.
Mitigation of thermal-expansion mismatch enhances interfacial bonding.
A clean, minimally oxidized, microrough copper surface is suitable for coating adhesion.
A graded Ni-based interlayer promotes interdiffusion between the copper substrate and AlCoCrFeNi coating.
Controlled processing temperatures, including substrate preheating, enable diffusion and interlayer formation.
An inert or vacuum atmosphere prevents oxidation during coating deposition.
Controlled thermal interdiffusion creates a gradual compositional variation across the interface.
Gradual compositional variation enhances mechanical interlocking at the interface.
Enhanced mechanical interlocking strengthens coating adhesion.
The graded interlayer improves wear resistance relative to direct deposition without an interlayer.
The graded interlayer significantly improves adhesion relative to direct deposition without an interlayer.
Incorrect deposition parameters, temperature, or interlayer thickness can cause insufficient interdiffusion or over-diffusion.
Insufficient interdiffusion or over-diffusion adversely affects adhesion or wear performance.
